findings.observation: The final local build now completes the governed source, relationship, evidence review, current state, Wiki, People, separate action approval, verified local destination, unknown-result reconciliation, refresh, no-action, supersession, and deletion loops. The deployed site still exposes no usable sign-in method, so a working recruiter cannot enter this system outside the isolated evaluation account.
findings.evidence: docs/evaluations/2026-08-11-system-ui-click-acceptance-002.json; local Playwright session ts-99-r4; production session ts-99-live-002.
findings.user_impact: The candidate Web workflow is coherent and substantially usable, but the sellable service is unreachable and has no proven cross-day operating continuity.
findings.recommendation: Deploy behind a usable authenticated pilot account, then run the same governed relationship across a real elapsed day without database repair.
findings.verification: A consented recruiter enters production, completes the loop, returns the next day to the same current state and history, and recovers from one failed capture without duplicate work.

findings.criterion: Paid value in ordinary recruiting work
findings.observation: The UI reduces reconstruction burden in the synthetic workflow and keeps one next action calm and reviewable, but no working recruiter has yet compared it with their existing notes, CRM, or ATS over repeated searches.
findings.evidence: The current matrix is synthetic and system-focused; it contains no consented repeated-use field outcome or willingness-to-pay evidence.
findings.user_impact: Operational usability is plausible, while recurring value and price tolerance remain hypotheses.
findings.recommendation: Run a small concierge pilot with explicit success measures for time-to-reconstruct, missed follow-up reduction, correction cost, and voluntary continued use.
findings.verification: At least three authorized recruiters repeat the workflow in ordinary searches and prefer continuing at an explicit pilot price without safety workarounds.

strengths: The same-name comparison preserves assignment context instead of collapsing people by name.
Current understanding, exact evidence, prior versions, one action, and outcome now form one comprehensible desktop loop.
Deletion removes the final relationship cleanly and returns the recruiter to a non-stale workspace.
No-action is a durable, intentional outcome rather than an empty screen.
missing_evidence: Usable authenticated production entry and production build parity.
Capture retry, duplicate submission, stale expiry, restore-to-review, and real cross-day return through the Web UI.
Repeated-use value and willingness-to-pay evidence from consented working recruiters.
open_questions: Does the candidate workflow save enough relationship-reconstruction time over a week to earn an explicit paid-pilot commitment?
